'''Isaak Bacharach''' (2 December 1854  – 22 September 1942) was a German [[mathematics]] professor in [[Erlangen]] who proved the [[Cayley–Bacharach theorem]] on intersections of [[cubic curve]]s.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Bacharach | first1=I. | title=Ueber den Cayley'schen Schnittpunktsatz | publisher=Springer|location=Berlin and Heidelberg | year=1886 | journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] | issn=0025-5831 | volume=26 | issue=2 | pages=275–299 | url=http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/PPN235181684_0026/PPN235181684_0026___LOG_0035.pdf | doi=10.1007/BF01444338| s2cid=120983080 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first1=David|last1=Eisenbud|first2=Mark|last2=Green|first3=Joe|last3=Harris | title=Cayley-Bacharach theorems and conjectures | journal=Bulletin of the AMS | volume=33 | pages=295–324 | year=1996 | issue=3 | doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-96-00666-0 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

He was murdered at the [[Theresienstadt Ghetto|Theresienstadt concentration camp]] during [[The Holocaust]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bacharach Isaak: Death Certificate, Ghetto Terezín|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121128162848/http://109.123.214.108/en/document/DOCUMENT.ITI.5628|archive-date=28 November 2012|url=http://109.123.214.108/en/document/DOCUMENT.ITI.5628|website=Holocaust.cz}}</ref>
